findings.title: Backup code consumed non-atomically, allowing reuse via concurrent logins
findings.body: The backup code is verified by reading the encrypted list, then writing back the list with the used entry nulled in a separate update. Two concurrent login requests with the same valid code can both read the unmodified list, both pass the indexOf check, and both succeed. A single-use code can therefore be replayed. The check and consumption need to be atomic (e.g., conditional update or transaction with compare-and-swap on the stored value).

findings.title: Used backup code is set to null but the code list is never pruned, and indexOf on null entries is fragile
findings.body: Consumed entries are replaced with null in the array. Subsequent submissions of an empty or null-like input can match nulls in indexOf only if the input is null, and the request body backupCode is only checked for truthiness, so this is mostly safe; however the stored array keeps nulls forever and the JSON shape changes from string[] to (string|null)[], which the disable endpoint and any future reader must handle. Consider removing the entry instead.

findings.title: Backup code verified without requiring 2FA enabled path to be sane; wrong input type can crash
findings.body: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll is called on whatever the client sends. If backupCode is a non-string truthy value (number, object), replaceAll throws a TypeError causing a 500 instead of a 400. Also JSON.parse of decrypted data is unguarded.

findings.title: Backup code used to disable 2FA is never consumed
findings.body: The comment says the codes are deleted at the end, and the update sets backupCodes to null, so this does clear them on success. However the disable path with a backup code does not check that the code is still unused before the update, so concurrent requests can each disable 2FA with the same code; combined with the non-atomic pattern this is replay-prone. Same race as login.

findings.title: Setup overwrites backup codes and stores them before 2FA is enabled, and returns them without a confirmation gate
findings.body: Backup codes are written to the DB during setup while twoFactorEnabled stays false. Each setup call regenerates and replaces codes, which is intended, but the codes are shown to the user before they are verified and a backup code login path in login/next-auth checks only twoFactorEnabled, so this is acceptable only if the enable step is required. Additionally, symmetricEncrypt is called with process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY which is checked earlier, so ok; the real concern is that the plaintext codes are returned in the setup JSON response and cached by any intermediary.

findings.title: Backup code blob URL is created on every setup and the previous one revoked by a stale closure
findings.body: backupCodesUrl is read from component state inside handleSetup, so if state is stale the previous object URL may not be revoked, leaking blob URLs. The revoke condition relies on the previous render's value rather than a ref.

findings.title: formatBackupCode is used before its declaration in handleSetup's closure order and the backup codes state is untyped
findings.body: useState([]) gives an implicitly any[] state type, and formatBackupCode is a const declared after handleSetup; it works at call time but the untyped state hides shape errors. backupCodes should be typed as string[].

findings.title: Closing the dialog after a backup code display does not reset the flow when the modal is dismissed via overlay
findings.body: The Close button resets state, but dismissing the Dialog via onOpenChange (escape or overlay) skips resetState, so the backup codes step and the codes remain in state and the user can reopen into the DisplayBackupCodes step with stale codes.

findings.title: Backup code login errors are mapped but the backup code field is never cleared, and password is still required
findings.body: On an IncorrectBackupCode error, the form stays on the backup step with the old value; the errorMessages fallback and new branches are inconsistent with the errorMessages map used elsewhere. Also the 'Lost access' button clears only totpCode, not the password-related state, so the form submits with stale values.

findings.title: resetForm called after success clears password field values but leaves the modal state stale on error paths
findings.body: On failure paths the entered backup code or TOTP code is not cleared, so after an incorrect code the user must manually clear inputs; combined with the shared form, toggling Lost access does not clear errorMessage consistently.

findings.title: Backup code login path bypasses the password check requirement ordering and TOTP fallback
findings.body: When a backup code is supplied and the user has 2FA enabled, the TOTP branch is skipped entirely, but the earlier password check only runs when no totpCode is present. A request with totpCode and backupCode both present but no password skips password verification for CAL users whose password is set, since the password check is gated on !credentials.totpCode. The backup code path then succeeds without any password, which is an authentication bypass for users who know only a backup code and an email.

findings.title: Migration adds column without considering existing 2FA users
findings.body: Existing users who already have 2FA enabled get backupCodes null, so the backup code path returns MissingBackupCodes and they have no recovery path other than TOTP. This should be documented or the UI should prompt regeneration.

findings.title: Backup code instruction text is inaccurate for the setup screen
findings.body: backup_code_instructions says codes can be used to grant access without the authenticator, but it is also used as the description of the setup backup codes step, where the user is not told to save them now or that they are shown only once.

findings.title: No test covers backup code login or the incorrect backup code path
findings.body: The PR's stated test plan is to log in with backup codes, but no e2e test exercises that flow; the only new tests cover the setup download/copy and close buttons. The checklist also states no tests prove the feature works.
